title: Personal LLM inference mini-sheet (Connor Patel)
content:
Mini-sheet - personal tracking + quick metrics (rough)

Goal: quick nightly mini-tracker for small inference experiments. Fast comparisons so I can decide which quant/model combo to push to the internal perf harness. Not a canonical bench — do not use for SLOs.

Table (columns: experiment | model | quant | batch | seq | avg_lat_ms | p95_ms | throughput_tok_s | cost_per_1k_tok | notes)
exp-2026-02-18-a | llama2-13b | q4f16 | 1 | 512 | 82 | 120 | 430 | $0.75 | baseline-ish, occasional repetition on long tails
exp-2026-02-18-b | llama2-13b | q8_0 | 1 | 512 | 70 | 95 | 500 | $0.60 | lower latency, slightly worse tokenization artifacts
exp-2026-02-19-a | gptj-6b | q4f16 | 1 | 512 | 45 | 68 | 880 | $0.30 | good tradeoff small models for latency-sensitive routes
exp-2026-02-20-a | redwood-small-3b | q4_0 | 2 | 256 | 28 | 42 | 1200 | $0.18 | using batching=2 improves throughput, quality fine for short prompts
exp-2026-02-22-a | llama2-13b | q4f16 | 4 | 512 | 160 | 240 | 1200 | $0.50 | high batch to test throughput, tail latency high (not for interactive)

Method notes:
- Measurements done on dev-dedicated-1 (A100 equivalent) with local harness (script: tools/mini-bench.sh).
- Prompt set: 40 prompts, seq len = average 450 (varies), measure token-level throughput and embed cost model.
- avg_lat_ms = mean end-to-end response ms for full prompt+gen; p95 from 40 samples (so noisy).
- cost_per_1k_tok: rough unit economics using current hosted price table + gpu runtime estimate (not precise).

Quick findings (rough):
- q8_0 on llama2-13b gives meaningful latency wins with small quality degradation — candidate for staging route with QA prompts.
- gptj-6b is surprisingly good for short interactive flows; low latency + low cost. Consider canary for low-Q routes.
- Batching helps throughput a lot but tails explode; need to test with target SLO workload (50k req/day sim).

TODO / next steps:
- [ ] Re-run p95 with 200 prompts to reduce noise (assign to me, Connor)
- [ ] Add mixing test (route selector) to validate fallback quality for q8_0 variant (Maya to help)
- [ ] Convert best-run configs into perf-harness PR (github.com/redwood-inference/prs/123)
- [ ] Estimate infra cost delta for switching low-cost route in prod (quick calc in sheet)

Open questions / notes to self:
- Need a better way to normalize cost_per_1k across quant and batch — current calc underestimates memory overhead.
- Is q8_0 deterministic for our eval prompts? saw two runs with different hallucination patterns; might be sampling seed-related.
- Talk to SRE about tail mitigation (pre-warm, soft-priority queues) before any high-batch rollout.

Links / refs:

- Perf harness PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prs/123
- Slack: #serving-runtime thread: message ts 1677000000

Rough scratch notes (raw):
- If we can get q8_0 stable -> ~20% unit cost reduction on 13B routes (estimate).
- Consider gating q8_0 behind a quality monitor (automated eval on daily prompt set).
- Remember: these mini-sheets are operationally noisy — reconcile with full bench before permanent changes.

-- Connor (keeping this short; will push cleaned results to /team/eng/applied-ml/perf/bench-2026)
